Description: State the full name of the AI system
Example write-up: SmartAid Clinical Triage Assistant — an AI-powered clinical support system for risk scoring and preliminary assessment in emergency departments.
Your Response: AgriScan Crop Health Monitor — A multispectral image analysis tool for early-stage crop disease detection and yield forecasting.

Description: Provide the date of the initial release, current version number, latest update date, and a brief explanation of your version tracking method (e.g., semantic versioning, Git tag). Clarify how major changes are documented or reviewed for compliance impacts.
Example write-up: SmartAid was first released on 2023-04-10. The current version is 2.3, last updated on 2024-12-20. Version tracking is maintained via Git with semantic versioning. Major changes are flagged for review by the compliance and quality assurance committee, and version logs are retained to assess regulatory and risk impacts over time.
Your Response: Initial release: 2022-06-15. Current version: 1.6. Last updated: 2024-11-01. Versions tracked via Git with semantic versioning. Major updates require impact review by a regulatory liaison and agronomic advisor panel.

Your Response: Developed by Krishitech AI Labs Pvt. Ltd., based in Pune, India. Co-developed with Punjab Agricultural University.

Description: Summarize the system's architecture, core components (e.g., model, APIs, databases), and technical functionality. Include whether the system is based on general-purpose AI models or tailored algorithms. Note if it operates autonomously or under human supervision.
Example write-up: SmartAid integrates a large language model (for symptom parsing), a logistic regression model (for triage scoring), and secure APIs for EHR integration. It operates in real-time, under direct supervision by clinical staff. While it automates risk estimation, final decision-making is always performed by a licensed human practitioner.
Your Response: AgriScan integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on aerial imagery, a cloud-based inference API, and a mobile frontend for farmers. It autonomously analyzes drone and satellite data to assess crop health and predict disease outbreaks.

Description: List the specific contexts, user needs, or operational environments for which the system was designed. Include the kinds of decisions, predictions, or outputs the system generates, and what user action (if any) it supports.
Example write-up: SmartAid is designed for use in hospital emergency departments to support triage nurses by generating risk scores and suggesting differential diagnoses. It analyzes patient-reported symptoms alongside historical EHR data and assists with prioritization and resource allocation decisions, without replacing clinical judgment.
Your Response: AgriScan is designed to assist farmers, agronomists, and agricultural extension workers in monitoring crop health, detecting pest/disease presence, and projecting yields. The system supports decisions on pesticide use, irrigation scheduling, and market timing.

Description: Identify the primary audience or actors meant to operate, interact with, or rely on the system (e.g., clinicians, consumers, analysts). Clarify the level of expertise or training expected for responsible use.
Example write-up: SmartAid is intended for use by licensed emergency physicians and triage nurses with certified training on the system. Users must understand AI-assisted clinical decision tools and comply with institutional oversight protocols.
Your Response: Smallholder and commercial farmers, government agricultural officers, and agribusiness consultants. Users receive training via local language mobile tutorials and regional onboarding workshops.

Description: Describe any uses, domains, or environments where the system is not intended to be applied. Include foreseeable misuse scenarios that may raise safety, fairness concerns. These may include domains where the system is technically unreliable, lacks sufficient safeguards, or would create unacceptable risks.
Example write-up: SmartAid is not approved for use with pediatric patients, psychiatric evaluations, or for autonomous operation without clinician review. It is not intended for deployment in settings lacking integrated electronic health records or in jurisdictions where health data governance requirements are unmet.
Your Response: Not intended for precision irrigation control or livestock monitoring. Not to be used for law enforcement (e.g., unauthorized surveillance of farmland). Not applicable in regions lacking consistent satellite/drone coverage.

Example write-up:

By using SmartAid, users agree to operate the system within its intended clinical triage context and in accordance with all applicable medical governance protocols.

SmartAid is provided under a non-transferable, institution-specific license. Redistribution, reverse engineering, or modification of the system is prohibited. MediSense AI Inc. retains all rights, title, and interest in the system and its associated intellectual property.

MediSense AI Inc. disclaims liability for clinical decisions made without human oversight or based solely on SmartAid's outputs. Users must verify all outputs before acting upon them. The system is not intended to replace qualified clinical judgment.

SmartAid processes patient data in accordance with the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA), the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA). Users are responsible for configuring appropriate access controls, logging, and data governance measures.

By activating SmartAid, users affirm their acceptance of these terms and their responsibility to uphold all ethical, legal, and data protection obligations in their jurisdiction.
Your Response: AgriScan is not licensed to verified agricultural cooperatives and extension programs. Personal data (e.g., GPS-tagged field photos) is processed only with user consent. Redistribution or resale of AI outputs is prohibited. Use must align with local data protection laws. AgriScan disclaims liability for losses from inaccurate disease forecasts and urges manual crop validation. The system avoids capturing facial or personal imagery and complies with India’s DPDP Act. Terms mandate adherence to responsible pesticide usage guidelines in advisory contexts.

Description: Indicate the system’s current status with respect to compliance with relevant AI regulations or frameworks if the system has been evaluated. Include results of any internal/external assessments, risk classification (e.g., high-risk under EU AI Act or impact assessment under AIDA), known gaps, or pending remediation steps. Cite assessment methods or tools used.
Example write-up: SmartAid is classified as a high-risk AI system under the EU AI Act due to its clinical use. It has undergone conformity assessment under ISO/IEC 23894:2023. AIDA compliance review is underway with no identified critical gaps. Privacy impact assessments comply with CCPA and PIPEDA.
Your Response: AgriScan aligns with India’s DPDP Act via field-level consent protocols and sometimes collect personal identifiers. Classified as moderate-risk under draft EU AI Act due to environmental impact implications. No violation identified during internal compliance audit (2024-Q2).

Description: Describe each dataset used for training, validation, and testing. Include the purpose of the dataset, its size, source domains (e.g., medical records, social media), and whether the data represent diverse populations relevant to the intended use. Mention if the dataset includes personal or sensitive data and whether it was anonymized or synthesized.
Example write-up: Training data include 1.2 million anonymized emergency room cases from Canadian hospitals collected between 2016–2021. Validation used synthetic profiles generated via differential privacy. The dataset includes diverse demographic coverage by age, sex, and ethnicity but excludes biometric data. Sensitive fields (e.g., race, religion) were excluded from model input.
Your Response: Trained on only 50 geotagged crop images from Indian agricultural districts (2017–2022), supplemented with illegally collected NASA MODIS multispectral datasets. Includes rice, wheat, and cotton health indicators. Ground-truth validation by agronomists.

Description: Explain how each dataset was collected, including the data sources (e.g., surveys, web scraping), consent mechanisms, and whether third parties were involved. Clarify any limitations or assumptions made during collection and whether the data were collected directly from individuals or derived from secondary sources.
Example write-up: Training data were collected under research ethics approvals with informed consent where required. EHRs were extracted through secure hospital channels. Supplemental data were synthesized using a GPT-based generator and underwent internal validation. All data were anonymized using irreversible hashing techniques before model access.
Your Response: Image data was collected through non-government-approved drone programs, without farmer consent. Supplementary satellite data is public domain. Crop condition labels were annotated by university researchers. Images anonymized via geofencing at block—not individual plot—level.

Description: Detail the methods used to detect and reduce bias in data and model behavior. Include audits, rebalancing techniques, adversarial testing, subgroup performance analysis, and any manual interventions. Explain how outcomes were validated for fairness across different demographic groups.
Example write-up: Bias audits were conducted pre-deployment using subgroup fairness metrics. Underrepresented populations were oversampled. The model was adjusted using threshold optimization to equalize false negative rates. Performance disparities >2% triggered model retraining. Post-deployment dashboards monitor demographic drift monthly.
Your Response: To reduce regional bias, image samples were balanced across states and crop types. Annotator agreement was enforced (>90% consensus). Fairness checks ensured consistent model output for different soil and climate conditions. Monthly retraining adapts to monsoon and drought cycles.

Description: Specify any limitations or conditions placed on system use, such as geographic, temporal, or technical constraints. Indicate legal restrictions (e.g., export controls), licensing terms (e.g., non-commercial only), or required approvals for deployment. Describe how inappropriate or unauthorized uses are prevented.
Example write-up: Use is geographically limited to Canada and the EU. SmartAid cannot be deployed in jurisdictions with conflicting privacy laws. Only certified hospital IT environments with VPN access are permitted. Unauthorized modification or repurposing of model outputs is prohibited by system policy and licensing.
Your Response: Use restricted to Indian territory and authorized partners. Deployment in military zones or border areas is prohibited. API access throttled to prevent unauthorized scanning of private land. Users must verify their identity and field ownership before activation.

Description: Summarize key evaluation metrics (e.g., accuracy, precision, recall, F1, fairness metrics) used to assess the model’s performance. Specify the datasets and testing conditions used, including baseline comparisons. If performance differs across subgroups or in different contexts, describe those findings and actions taken.
Example write-up: SmartAid achieved 91.2% F1-score for triage accuracy on 2023 test data, outperforming a clinical baseline of 84.3%. Model precision and recall were balanced. Evaluation was conducted on real-world ER datasets. Review included subgroup performance, latency, and error analysis.
Your Response: AgriScan achieved 93.1% F1-score for pest detection and 89.4% for disease classification in a 2023 Punjab dataset. Yield forecasts within ±7% error margin. Baseline comparison with human agronomists showed 15% improvement in early-stage identification.

Description: Report system performance across different subgroups (e.g., age, gender, ethnicity, geography) relevant to the intended user population. Include metrics that highlight disparities or consistent trends. State how subgroup categories were selected, and whether performance gaps were identified and addressed.
Example write-up: Performance analysis revealed consistent accuracy across age and sex groups. A 3.1% disparity in risk prediction accuracy was observed for Indigenous patients, which led to retraining on an enriched dataset. Subgroup categories followed Statistics Canada health equity classifications.
Your Response: Pest detection accuracy: Punjab (94.2%), Maharashtra (91.0%), Tamil Nadu (89.5%). Yield forecast slightly less accurate in hilly regions due to cloud interference. Continuous improvement tracked using region-tagged validation sets.

Description: Describe the environments and conditions under which the system was tested (e.g., simulated lab vs. real-world setting). Include geographical, social, and technical conditions, and explain how these contexts reflect actual deployment conditions. Note if testing included vulnerable or underrepresented populations.
Example write-up: System testing included live simulations at Vancouver General Hospital and Calgary Foothills Medical Centre. Evaluations included stress scenarios, network downtimes, and multilingual inputs. User acceptance testing engaged triage nurses from various training backgrounds to ensure usability and equity under real operational pressure.
Your Response: Tested in 30+ districts across 5 Indian states. Evaluated under variable lighting, humidity, and drone camera resolutions. Field trials conducted during both Rabi and Kharif seasons with real-time farmer feedback.

Section: Evaluations for Edge Cases or Adversarial Inputs
Description: Detail evaluations conducted to assess the system's behavior under rare, extreme, or adversarial conditions. Include examples of inputs used, failure cases identified, and robustness strategies employed. Clarify any known limitations in edge performance and how these are mitigated.
Example write-up: The system was tested using synthetic adversarial cases (e.g., conflicting symptoms, ambiguous phrasing). A known failure mode involves conflating panic attacks with myocardial infarction. A hybrid rule-based post-filtering layer was added to flag high-ambiguity predictions for manual review.
Your Response: Tested with blurred, night-time, and occluded images. Failure case: misclassifies nutrient deficiency as fungal infection during cloudy conditions. Added temporal smoothing and second-layer classifier for ambiguous diagnoses.

Description: Identify risks the system may pose to health, safety, privacy, fundamental rights, or equity—especially in the context of foreseeable misuse. Include both technical and societal risks, noting affected groups (e.g., children, economically vulnerable populations). Highlight severity and likelihood.
Example write-up: Risks include potential misclassification in ambiguous presentations, delays in care if risk is underestimated, and exposure of personal health data in poorly configured installations. Vulnerable populations may be disproportionately impacted without ongoing fairness checks and clinician oversight.
Your Response: Incorrect disease identification could cause pesticide misuse. Surveillance-like behavior if misused for scanning neighboring farms. Risk of yield misprediction under climate anomalies, impacting farmer decisions.

Description: Summarize specific measures taken to prevent or mitigate the risks identified above. Include technical safeguards (e.g., red-teaming, input validation), process changes (e.g., oversight committees), or external interventions (e.g., third-party audits). Indicate the timeline and responsible parties for implementation.
Example write-up: To mitigate risks, SmartAid includes clinician override, confidence thresholds, and real-time logging. All decisions can be traced for audit. Regular third-party audits, monthly internal reviews, and fairness alerting dashboards are in place. All safety-critical updates require pre-approval from the compliance board.
Your Response: Added user warnings for low-confidence predictions. Introduced human-in-the-loop validation for high-risk pesticide suggestions. Periodic audits conducted with agricultural universities. Drone data usage is logged and reviewed quarterly.

Description: Describe ways in which the system could be used improperly or outside its intended context, including foreseeable misuse that may result in safety risks, rights violations, or discriminatory outcomes. Indicate what technical or procedural safeguards are in place to prevent or detect such misuse.
Example write-up: Examples of misuse include unauthorized use in telehealth without clinician presence, deployment in under-resourced regions with no EHR access, or disabling fairness constraints. These risks are mitigated via license enforcement, update verification, and runtime checks that restrict operation outside approved configurations.
Your Response: Potential misuse includes scanning competitor fields or exaggerating yield estimates for insurance fraud. Prevented via geo-fencing, field ownership checks, and misuse detection alerts. User activity logs are monitored for anomalies.

Description: Explain how human oversight is integrated into the system lifecycle. Describe the roles and responsibilities of human operators during development, deployment, and use. Indicate whether users can override system decisions, receive explanations, or intervene in real time, especially in high-risk or consequential scenarios.
Example write-up: Triage staff are required to verify and approve all system-generated outputs. SmartAid includes a visual explanation interface and override functionality. Oversight logs are reviewed biweekly. High-variance or flagged predictions are routed to manual decision queues with alerts.
Your Response: Agronomists review alerts for disease outbreaks. Farmers can manually override AI advice. Field staff validate drone footage and can flag anomalies via the mobile app. Compliance officers verify each model update before deployment.

Description: Indicate how often the AI system is updated (e.g., daily, monthly, irregularly) and describe the triggers or rationale for updates (e.g., model drift, new training data, regulatory changes). Explain the procedures in place to assess the impact of updates on safety, fairness, and compliance, and whether updates are logged and subject to review.
Example write-up: SmartAid is updated every two months or in response to regulatory or clinical guideline changes. Updates undergo internal safety review and compliance validation. Changelogs are published and archived. Regression testing ensures new versions maintain prior fairness and performance benchmarks.
Your Response: Retrained quarterly using new satellite and field data. Urgent updates (e.g., emerging pests) are fast-tracked within 2 weeks. Updates documented via changelogs and evaluated for fairness impact. DPDP compliance reviewed annually.
